newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end lower, seen opening steady.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end lower, seen opening steady.

text.p: Chilean blue chips broke a two-session rally to close lower on Wall Street's volatility and a streak of profit-taking, but the market should hold steady at the opening, said traders.
"The bolsa should remain relatively flat. Even though the bourse has rallied this week, there's no news to point to any structural change," said one dealer.
The 40-share IPSA index ended down 0.52 percent at 98.97 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.5 percent to 5,446.08 points. Volume was 12.3 billion pesos, similar to Tuesday's levels.
Traders said the light volume showed institutional investors were not yet returning in force to the market, despite a recent fall in long term interest rates.
"There's not yet been any fundamental restructuring which will persuade them to switch funds from fixed income," said one dealer.
Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts closed mixed on Wall Street's early slide, which also undermined other major Latin American markets.
Electricity and forestry stocks, which had rallied earlier in the week, fell as investors cashed in gains, said traders.
Power utility Enersis shed 0.78 percent to 254 pesos, while pulp-maker Copec declined 0.79 percent to 1,761 pesos.
Winners included winery Concha y Toro, up 1.9 percent at 161 pesos, telecoms company Telex, up 0.87 percent at 1,160 pesos and Banco O'Higgins, which rose 0.64 percent to 1,580 pesos.
